items.description: The `ArgoCDTools` repo exists with content: the presync entrypoint, its support code and the Dockerfile. `/work/ArgoCDTools` had an origin and no commits at planning time.

The entrypoint clones the deploy repo at the SHA it is handed, and authenticates that clone via an inline credential helper rather than a token-in-URL remote — deliberately unlike `support/iac-agent/bin/iac-impl:372-383`, so the PAT never reaches the process table or an echoed remote.

terraform-backend-git runs on 127.0.0.1:6061 inside the pod against the same state repository and keying `iac` uses (D32), started by the same recipe as `support/iac-agent/bin/iac-impl:309-350` including the GIT_API_TOKEN → GITHUB_TOKEN mapping at `:322`.

`terraform init && terraform apply` run in the clone's `terraform/` with `config/<stage>/*.tfvars` read from that same clone (D14) — no tfvars travel through Argo. The backend address, lock_address and unlock_address are passed as `-backend-config` at init against a deploy repo's bare `backend "http" {}`, the pattern at `/work/HelmCharts/tools/deploy/deploy_cli/tf.py:59-68` and `:139-151`, under the state key scheme `argocd/<repo>/<stage>/terraform.tfstate`.

The PV reattach (D29) finds `Released` PVs whose `claimRef` names the destination namespace it was handed — and only that namespace — and nulls out `claimRef.uid` and `resourceVersion` so they return to `Available` pre-bound, the same fix as `/work/HelmCharts/tools/deploy/deploy_cli/helmops.py:117-153`. Exercised against a deliberately-`Released` PV on the dev cluster (ruled proof bar), and written to work under the Job's own ServiceAccount in-cluster as well as from this pod.

Exit-code discipline holds (D30): the entrypoint exits non-zero on any failure in the flow and never exits zero on a partial success. Proven from this pod against a throwaway deploy repo and a scratch state key on both the success and the deliberate-failure path (ruled proof bar).

App Terraform reaches its secrets through the `!bao` resolver, not a Terraform vault provider: the entrypoint logs into OpenBao with the dedicated AppRole and resolves `!bao kv/<path>#<key>` refs into environment variables before running Terraform, mirroring `support/iac-agent/bin/iac-impl:108-134` and `:159-179` and hard-failing on any unresolvable ref. No vault/openbao provider joins the estate's provider set and no app-authored Terraform handles the AppRole.

The estate-wide baseline manifest ships in the image, declared as `support/iac-agent/etc/iac/secrets.example.yaml` declares its entries, and a deploy repo's optional `config/<stage>/secrets.yaml` merges over it. Because the baseline is committed repo content — unlike `iac`'s never-committed `/etc/iac/secrets.yaml` — nothing unsafe in git is a literal in it, including the age recipient.

The image carries Terraform, terraform-backend-git, git, the scripts and the baseline manifest and nothing else (D31), with Terraform unpinned from the hashicorp `noble` suite as `support/iac-image/Dockerfile:100-115` installs it and terraform-backend-git pinned to v0.1.11 as `:129-130` pins it. It can reach `https://secrets.home/` and the provider network mirror — the homelab root CA is trusted by both the system and Python, and Terraform's mirror configuration for `registry.terraform.io/pvginkel/*` is present.
CI publishes `registry:5000/argocd-hook:<n>` from a push to `main` on the `IaC/ArgoCDTools` job, and a build has actually run and produced an image.

The default hook-image pin lands in the library chart's values and names the tag the first successful `IaC/ArgoCDTools` build actually published. Where the build number was not knowable at phase time, the plan's `"1"` is confirmed or the correction is recorded as owed, given published `dist/` tarballs are immutable.

items.area: R2 — the two repos' first releases
items.description: The entrypoint's argument contract and the library chart's Job template agree: the chart passes the destination namespace as a fourth `required`-guarded argument alongside repo, revision and stage (`/work/Charts/charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:41-44`), and the entrypoint takes it as given. `homelab-shared` publishes as 0.2.0 with a new committed tarball, and the render gate's assertions and fixture moved with it (`/work/Charts/tests/render-consumer.sh:62-68`, `:104-106`; `/work/Charts/tests/consumer/values.yaml:37-40`).

OpenBao gains a dedicated AppRole for app-infra Terraform, not srviac's `iac-agent` (D33). Its policy grants the `argocd-hooks/*` prefix glob for the hook's own namespace plus explicit enumeration of every leaf outside it that the baseline manifest resolves — the shape of `openbao_iac_agent_kv_paths` at `ansible/inventories/prd/group_vars/openbao.yml:118-124`. The new consumer joins every place the openbao role enumerates consumers by name, including the rotation-run credential staging at `ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/approle.yml:408-455`.

`argocd-hook-credentials` carries exactly `OPENBAO_URL`, `OPENBAO_ROLE_ID`, `OPENBAO_SECRET_ID` and `GIT_API_TOKEN`, with `GIT_USERNAME` a fixed literal (`x-access-token`) outside the Secret, and the four values live under a `kv/eso/prd/...` path so slice 009's ESO leaves can read them under the existing `eso/prd/*` grant (`ansible/inventories/prd/group_vars/openbao.yml:96`) with no policy change. Everything else the hook needs resolves from OpenBao at runtime — the Job supplies no `env:` at all (`/work/Charts/charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:45-47`).

The scoped git token's required permissions are specified for the operator's mint: `pvginkel/TerraformState` read-write, the deploy repos read, and webhook administration (`admin:repo_hook` per D39/D41). Where GitHub's token model cannot express the deploy-repos-read-only half in one token, that is stated as an accepted, named over-grant rather than left implied.

The state encryption key is minted as the hook's own leaf in `kv/argocd-hooks/`, carrying the same age keypair `iac` uses today rather than a new one — `iac` and the hook write into the same TerraformState repository (D32) and phases.md B.4 moves existing state into the hook's key scheme, so a second keypair would make state written by one side undecryptable by the other. The duplication's rotation consequence is recorded, not discovered later.

No secret value was written by an agent. The hand-back gives the operator the exact `bao` commands and paths, the GitHub PAT permissions, and the `playbooks/site-openbao.yml` run the AppRole needs — and says plainly what remains owed rather than that it is done.

`support/iac-image/` and the `iac` image are untouched — D31 is explicit that the existing image stays as it is and gains no Argo-specific anything — and no chart was migrated to the library chart nor anything backported to HelmCharts (D16, D43).
